A third-order linear simulation (poles at $-1,-10,-20$ rad/s, 20 seeds) shows that co-contraction cannot be left on as a stability crutch. A learner that stays stiff and first-order (S3) never recovered the true plant (0\% to criterion, asymptotic relative impulse error 0.41). Random trial-to-trial co-contraction (S5) likewise failed (0\%). Learners that recruited the transient modes did recover the plant: deep-end third-order identification from trial one (S1) in 7.0 trials (100\%), staged order-recruitment (S2) in 24.3 trials (100\%), and a bandwidth-only curriculum (S4) in 26.1 trials. On this linear plant the deep end is not slower than the curriculum; the result that matters for H0 is that refusing to relax leaves the transients unlearned.
